## Why

The K14 audit measured the copy drift: 126 requirement ids on `/`,
ungrouped 5+-digit figures, words joined at element boundaries
(`concern?<a`), bare `unknown`s, `camera sites` where observation-level
rows must read `records`. UXK14-5 lands the lints as a CI leg — but
**report-first**: the surfaces that own the flagged copy fix it under
their own tickets, so this row ships the linter, the corpus and the
flip mechanism, never the copy edits.

## What ships

- **`web/scripts/check-copy-lints.mjs`** — the copy linter. Corpus =
  `dist/page-types.json`, the P35.50 page-type manifest, so no built
  route escapes the sweep (the P35.50 dep's whole point). Rules over
  each route's `<main>` + `<footer>`:
  - **ids** — UUIDs, snake_case keys, raw enum tokens, requirement ids
    in prose (DR-C6-28 / SIG-UI-053's cited half): exempts `<code>` /
    `<pre>`, elements marked `data-technical-details` /
    `data-identifiers` (the SIG-UI-053 blocks — a forward contract for
    the surface rows) and `.sig-spec-refs` disclosures (SIG-UI-141).
  - **repeated-sentence** — an 8+-word sentence appearing twice in
    `main` + `footer` (SIG-UI-144; the "not a census" half stays a
    figure-component contract, not a text sweep).
  - **chrome-words** — footer words visible by default (details
    collapsed, nav labels excluded) over 40 (DR-K14-11's count shape).
  - **joined-punct / joined-boundary** — sentence-punctuation joins in
    extracted text and inline elements flush against a word,
    punctuation or each other in the built HTML (SIG-UI-153 /
    DR-K14-19 — the NEW-7 class).
  - **ungrouped-digits** — `\b\d{5,}\b` outside code, `<time>`, ids and
    dates (SIG-UI-153).
  - **bare-unknown** — a bare "unknown" in copy; typed absences name
    the kind.
  - **records-vs-sites** — "camera sites"/"listed cameras" outside a
    `data-sig-count="dedup"` element (the L3 CONF-07b interval
    contract) is a finding — and a dedup element that never names the
    site word is the reverse finding; a bare plural "cameras" joins
    the same rule (SIG-UI-063). `/glossary/` is exempt as the
    definitional surface.
  - **candidate-vs-provisional** — "provisional records" and
    "candidate value/estimate/count/figure/number/label" collapse the
    two axes (SIG-UI-062).
  - **vocabulary** — the lexicon's multi-word `not` phrasings
    ("observation-level record", "as of world", "resolved site", …)
    in prose.
  - **readability** — CP-8 advisory block (mean + longest sentence per
    page over the 22-word mean); prints, never fails.
- **`web/scripts/copy-lint-enforce.json`** — `sig.copy-lint-enforce/1`,
  the report→enforce map: `defaultMode: "report"`, `routes: {}`. A
  surface's ticket flips ITS registry pattern (or route path) to
  `"enforce"`, or `{"mode":"enforce","except":[rule-id]}` for a
  recorded bounded exemption it owns.
- **`web/package.json`** — `check:copy` wired into `npm run check`
  after `check:lexicon` (post-build, so the manifest exists). `ci.yml`
  untouched (CI-8).
- **`tests/unit/copy-lints.test.ts`** — 17 legs driving the real
  script over planted `page-types.json` manifests + planted pages:
  every rule fires on its planted violation and the compliant page
  passes; the report→enforce flip turns the same finding into a
  failure; `except` passes; vacuous = exit 3, missing manifest =
  exit 2 — never a silent green (SIG-ENG-042).
- **Coverage re-verdicts** — SIG-UI-063/144/153 `MISSING` →
  `MET-ENGINEERED(D-R10-PUBLISH-1)` (routing BL-085): the lint is
  engineered + fixture-verified; the per-surface enforce flips ride
  their own rows and the public-domain leg rides the publish
  deferral.
- **CHANGELOG** entry.

## Verify

- `npm --prefix web run check` — **green**: typecheck 0 errors; **734
  unit** (incl. `copy-lints.test.ts` 17 legs); internal build 51
  pages / 53 routes classified; lhci / licenses / paths / dom /
  figures / tokens / lexicon pass; **`check:copy` — 53 routes
  scanned, 278 report finding(s), 0 enforced** (the report-mode
  corpus printing the real known classes); **679 e2e** green incl.
  axe WCAG 2.2 AA.
- `make check` — recorded in the run ledger (env-local classes
  inherited where applicable).
- Head-bound CI — recorded as the `ci:` line in the run ledger +
  PHASE LOG.

## Not in this row

Fixing the flagged copy — each surface's own row (the report is the
punch-list; `copy-lint-enforce.json` is where each ticket records its
flip). The lexicon itself — P36.17 owns wording; the lints check
usage. The 40-word chrome budget's declared-strings half — P36.18's
`check-lexicon` leg already budgets `lexicon.chrome`; this row counts
the rendered footer.

## Deviations

Recorded in `docs/build/runs/P36.24.md`: the boundary join detector
grew the punctuation-before-tag and element-to-element shapes (the
`concern?<a` class slips a word-char-only regex); the readability
mean honestly counts the footer; `data-technical-details` /
`data-identifiers` / `data-sig-count="dedup"` are forward contracts
named by SIG-UI-053/063; the corpus includes internal + T3 routes (a
hand-maintained route list is the class the registry exists to
prevent); no ADR, no copy-batch rows — the lint ships no
reader-facing sentences.
